title: Exact joint eigenvalue densities of non-Hermitian random matrices are Calogero scattering states
authors: Zhenyu Xiao, Ze Chen, Yifei Liu, Shinsei Ryu
abstract: Determining exact joint eigenvalue densities is central to random matrix theory. We solve this long-standing problem for non-Hermitian matrices with transposition symmetry (complex symmetric and complex self-dual) at arbitrary matrix size. Up to a Vandermonde factor, they are scattering-state wave functions of the Calogero model, a line of particles interacting through an inverse-square potential, with the coupling strength set by the symmetry. In contrast to many previously known joint densities, the densities cannot be written as a gas of eigenvalues with pairwise interactions. We further compute the complex level spacing distributions and two-point spectral correlation functions, which carry power-law tails, absent in a Coulomb gas. Our results shed light on the interplay among random matrices, integrability, and symmetry.
summary: This work solves the long-standing problem of finding exact joint eigenvalue densities for non-Hermitian random matrices with specific symmetries. The key finding is that these densities are mathematically equivalent to the scattering states of the Calogero model. This reveals that the spectral statistics are governed by integrable dynamics, leading to power-law tails in correlation functions absent in simpler models.
main_problem: The paper determines the exact joint eigenvalue densities for non-Hermitian random matrices possessing transposition symmetry.
main_result: These joint densities are shown to be scattering-state wave functions of the Calogero model, revealing complex spectral statistics beyond simple Coulomb gas behavior.
method: The analysis involves solving differential equations derived from Gaussian integration by parts and relating the resulting structure to known integrable systems like the Calogero model.
model_or_system: The model consists of non-Hermitian random matrices belonging to three symmetry classes ($	ext{AI}^\dagger$, $	ext{A}$, $	ext{AII}^\dagger$). The underlying physics is governed by an eigenvalue problem whose structure is mapped onto the Calogero Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Joint eigenvalue density ($ho_C(z)$), nearest-neighbor spacing distribution ($p_{	ext{NN}}(s)$), and two-point spectral correlation functions.
important_parameters: The symmetry class dictates the Calogero coupling strength ($k$), which is crucial for determining the spectral behavior.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on identifying an underlying integrable structure (Calogero model) and making approximations in the collision limit for density calculations.
figures_summary: Figures compare origin-conditioned nearest-neighbor spacing distributions across different symmetry classes and show the asymptotic behavior of the spacing density.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem by defining the symmetry classes, derives the governing differential equations for the density, connects the solution to the Calogero scattering states, and analyzes specific observables like correlation functions and spacing distributions for each class.
why_interesting: The connection between random matrix theory, integrability (Calogero model), and spectral statistics provides deep insights into the underlying symmetries governing complex quantum systems, which is relevant to understanding spectral rigidity in quantum chaotic systems.
